label: GPT-6 Luna
output:
Lee,

I’ve been thinking about the dumper, and I reckon it’s worth us having a proper look at the numbers before we book another hire.

We hired a tracked dumper for 14 days this year at £85 a day, plus £30 delivery each time. That’s roughly £1,600 all in. There are already three patio digs and the Boughton drive booked for spring, so we’ll have work for one straight away. At this year’s use, the purchase price would be covered in about a year; even at half that use, roughly two years — before servicing and repairs, of course.

There’s a 2019 500kg tracked dumper for sale in Faversham for £1,650 ono. The seller says it had new tracks fitted last spring. If we split the purchase, that’s £825 each. We can keep it covered in my lean-to at the yard.

It’s not just the hire bill, either. In September, the hire place didn’t have one, so we barrowed six tonnes of muck at Hernhill. It took two extra days and your back was gone for a week. And when the delivery driver turned up at 11 one time, we lost half the morning. Having our own should make those jobs a bit easier to plan.

For running costs, I’d say we split servicing 50/50. If one of us breaks it, that person pays for the repair. If it doesn’t work out, we can sell it on — these seem to hold their value, so we’re not stuck with it.

We’ve known each other 15 years, so I want it to be straightforward and fair for both of us. Fancy coming to look at it with me this Saturday? At £1,650 ono, it’s worth seeing before someone else gets there.
